title: Third-Party Risk sub-page ignores project-level scoping — vendor-service returns full org-wide vendor data even when a projectId filter is requested
description:
**Files:** `vciso-service/src/routes/third-party-risk.routes.ts:218-227`
**Root Cause:** The route correctly resolves the caller's project-accessible `projectIds` via `filterAccessibleProjectIds` and forwards them to `crossService.fetchVendorDashboardRaw`/`fetchVendorAnalyticsRaw`/`fetchVendorReviewsDueRaw` as an outbound query param. The route's own code comment admits the gap directly: `// NOTE: projectIds is forwarded to vendor-service as an outbound query param ... but vendor-service's own route handlers are a separate repo/out of scope here — until it adds support for the param, these calls still return org-wide data.` So a user restricted to a subset of an org's projects (via PLAC) who opens the vCISO Third-Party Risk sub-page sees vendor risk data for every project in the organization, not just their own — the vciso-service-side scoping logic is correct but functionally inert because vendor-service (a separate repo) never honors the parameter.
**Impact:** A within-org, cross-project data over-exposure. On a platform where Project-Level Access Control (PLAC) is an actively-enforced isolation boundary elsewhere (evidence, risk, audit, trust-vault all PLAC-scope their own data), this sub-page silently bypasses that boundary for vendor/third-party risk data. Not a cross-organization leak, but a real project-isolation gap for any customer relying on PLAC to segment projects within one org.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
This fix spans two repos:

1. In vendor-service (separate repo — locate its dashboard/analytics/reviews-due route handlers): accept and apply an optional `projectIds` query param (comma-separated or repeated), filtering the underlying vendor query by `projectId: { $in: projectIds }` when supplied — mirroring how vciso-service's own CrossServiceIntegration.ts already sends the param.
2. Once vendor-service honors the param, no vciso-service change is needed — third-party-risk.routes.ts already forwards projectIds correctly; just remove the stale NOTE comment (lines 218-222) once verified.
3. Add an integration test: as a user restricted to Project A only, call GET the third-party-risk summary route and assert the returned vendor counts/scores match only Project A's vendors, not the org total.
```

title: No-project-selected state shows a fully zeroed layout with no proactive guidance across 5 of 7 vCISO sub-pages — two (Compliance Oversight, Third-Party Risk) give zero feedback of any kind, two (Strategic Planning, Risk Intelligence) only explain via a reactive toast after a failed action, only Executive Dashboard was originally checked
description:
**Files:** all 5 listed above -- this was originally logged (in an earlier, less thorough pass this same run) as an Executive-Dashboard-only Low defect; re-verified and broadened after checking the other sub-pages, which share the identical originating code comment `// No project selected — show empty/zeroed state instead of the organization-wide aggregate` almost verbatim (found in Executive Dashboard, Compliance Oversight, Third-Party Risk, Strategic Planning x2, Risk Intelligence -- clearly a copy-pasted pattern, not 5 independent implementations).
**Root Cause, by page:**
- Executive Dashboard (`page.jsx:216-227`): sets every metric to null/0/[] with zero corresponding UI message anywhere in the 2198-line file.
- Compliance Oversight (`page.jsx:131`) and Third-Party Risk (`page.jsx:201`): same zeroing pattern; a repo-wide grep for "select a project"/"choose a project" across both files returns zero matches -- no message exists anywhere, proactive or reactive.
- Strategic Planning (`page.jsx:269,338`): same zeroing pattern, but at least tracks a `noProjectSelected` boolean used to visually disable certain action buttons (opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed) -- better than nothing, but the only actual explanatory text is a reactive toast ("Select a project first", line ~3032) shown only after the user clicks the disabled-look budget-allocation button; nothing is shown proactively on page load.
- Risk Intelligence (`page.jsx:168`): identical to Strategic Planning -- a reactive toast ("Select a project first", line 401-402) only on attempting to create a FAIR scenario, nothing proactive.
- Board Reporting and AI Strategy Advisor: no instance of this comment/pattern found -- not confirmed to have the same gap, and not confirmed to be clean either; not deep-audited this run.
**Impact:** A fresh tenant, or any user who hasn't picked a project, sees what looks like real (and in 2 of 5 cases, alarmingly bad -- a literal 0 security score) computed data with no explanation across the majority of this module's primary pages, rather than an honest "Select a project to view this data" state. This is exactly the failure mode this module's own QA checklist calls out. Severity raised from Low to Medium given the breadth (5 of 7 sub-pages affected, not one).
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. Build one small shared component, e.g. <NoProjectSelectedState /> or a hook useProjectRequiredState(), that renders a consistent proactive banner: "Select a project above to view this data" (or "Set up your first project to get started" for a genuinely project-less fresh tenant) -- do not reimplement this per page a 6th and 7th time.
2. Wire it into Executive Dashboard, Compliance Oversight, and Third-Party Risk first (currently zero feedback of any kind).
3. Upgrade Strategic Planning and Risk Intelligence from reactive-toast-only to also show the same proactive banner on page load, keeping the existing toasts as a secondary reinforcement on blocked actions.
4. Verify Board Reporting and AI Strategy Advisor for the same gap -- not yet checked.
```

title: Zero action-level permission gating anywhere in the 33-file vCISO component tree — module relies entirely on one blanket layout-level `vciso.read` gate, so a read-only `vciso.read` grant (independently grantable per `ORG_ONLY_MODULE_PERMISSIONS`) renders every write action fully clickable
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action: every create/update/delete/approve button is wrapped in `PermissionGate`/`usePermission`, not just the page-level read gate.
**Files:** `(private)/vciso/layout.jsx` correctly wraps all 9 pages in one well-documented `<PermissionGate permission="vciso.read" allowProjectGrant>`. But a repo-wide grep for `PermissionHide`/`PermissionGate` across `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/vciso/` (33 files) returns zero matches — no sub-page or modal has any action-level check. Confirmed concretely: `strategic-planning/page.jsx` opens `InitiativeModal` (a full create/edit initiative form, lines 723/734/1375) and `board-reporting/page.jsx` opens `ReportGenerationModal` (lines 445/747/1392) with no permission check anywhere in either page or either modal component.
**Root Cause:** The module was built with a single coarse `vciso.read` layout gate and no follow-up pass adding action-level gates for the write/approve actions inside — unlike the backend, which correctly enforces the full `vciso.create`/`update`/`delete`/`approve`/`admin` action set per route (per this module's own `ORG_ONLY_MODULE_PERMISSIONS` entry: `vciso: ['read','create','update','delete','approve','admin']`, each independently grantable via the org-wide Extra Permissions modal).
**Impact:** Not a bypass — the backend still enforces the correct `vciso.*` action for each write route. But because `vciso.read` is independently grantable on its own (a realistic configuration: an org admin giving a board member or auditor read-only visibility into vCISO reporting without write access), that user sees fully clickable 'New Initiative', 'Generate Board Report', and every other write action across all 7 sub-modules, all of which will fail only after being clicked — an avoidable, module-wide UX inconsistency rather than an isolated one-page gap.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `<PermissionHide permission="vciso.create" allowProjectGrant>` (or `vciso.update`/`vciso.approve` as appropriate per action) around the trigger buttons for `InitiativeModal` (`strategic-planning/page.jsx`) and `ReportGenerationModal` (`board-reporting/page.jsx`) first, as the two highest-traffic write actions, then extend the same pattern to Compliance Oversight, Third-Party Risk, Risk Intelligence, and AI Strategy Advisor's own write/action triggers.

title: The vCISO layout's entire notification system (`notify`/`addNotification`/`dismissAlert`/`clearAlerts`, documented in the layout's own JSDoc usage example) is dead code — zero of the 9 vciso pages or any component ever calls it, so no vCISO lifecycle event ever produces an in-app notification
description:
**Checklist row:** §5.1 — Key lifecycle events dispatch a notification: assignment, due-date approaching/overdue, approval requested, approval decision, status change — each fires through the standard dispatch pipeline, not an ad hoc or silent path.
**Files:** `(private)/vciso/layout.jsx` builds a full `VCISOContext` exposing `notify`, `dismissAlert`, `clearAlerts` (backed by `vcisoSlice.js`'s `addNotification`/`dismissNotification`/`clearNotifications` reducers) and documents it in its own JSDoc usage example (`const { organizationId, notifications, notify } = useVCISO();`). A repo-wide grep for `.notify(` and `useVCISO()` destructuring across all 9 pages and all 33 components in `components/vciso/` shows every single call site destructures only `selectedProjectIds` — none destructures or invokes `notify`, `dismissAlert`, or `clearAlerts` anywhere. The context, reducer, and selectors are fully wired end-to-end but structurally unreachable from any real user action.
**Root Cause:** The notification scaffolding was built (context, Redux slice, JSDoc example) but never actually connected to any real lifecycle event — initiative creation/transition, report generation, advisor usage, etc. all complete with only a toast (a local, single-session UI acknowledgment) and none of them call the `notify()` helper the layout itself was built to provide.
**Impact:** No vCISO lifecycle event (new initiative assigned, board report generated and ready, AI advisor quota warning, initiative transitioned) produces any notification a user would see on return to the app or in another tab/session — unlike, for comparison, `intelli-audit`'s confirmed-working `_notifyAuditParticipants` pipeline for phase completion. A user who isn't actively watching the page at the moment something happens has no way to learn about it through this module.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Wire real call sites: in `strategic-planning/page.jsx`, after a successful `transitionInitiative`/initiative-create response, call `notify({ type: 'success', title: 'Initiative Updated', message: ... })` via the existing `useVCISO()` context (already imported in every page); in `board-reporting/page.jsx`, call it when `ReportGenerationModal` reports a completed generation. If the intent was always real cross-session notifications (not just an in-page banner), route these through the platform's standard BullMQ→Socket.IO notification pipeline instead (matching `intelli-audit`'s `_notifyAuditParticipants` pattern) rather than this local-only Redux slice.
